answer: Resist sybils with public contest windows: every new identity enters a review period where any peer may submit fraud evidence, like a bridge that only opens after inspectors check it. A vine of duplicate claims is easy to spot when all registrations hang in the open, each opal-tagged record visible to the whole network. If a challenge proves a fake, the identity is slashed and the challenger earns a bounty. An attacker minting ten thousand sybils must smuggle each one past open scrutiny, while an honest agent passes once and is done.
